name: Tax Identification Number (TIN)
note: Barbados's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: individuals aren't issued a TIN automatically; resident individuals must register with the Barbados Revenue Authority where section 52 of the Income Tax Act requires a return; the TIN is a unique, randomly generated 13-digit number starting with 1, digits only. Read as given on application, to residents. No check rule, age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Barbados: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Individuals are not automatically issued a TIN. Resident individuals are required to register with the Barbados Revenue Authority ... Barbados’ TIN is a unique 13 digital number. The number is randomly generated by the system. Each TIN starts with the number “1”.
